# Whole-fiber centered decompositions need not improve tail-root Jensen

This is an exact obstruction to one specific conditional-centroid proof
mechanism. Components may reweight whole fibers by arbitrary nonnegative
constants, but do not subdivide a fiber internally. It does not rule out
more general measurable or convex partitions within fibers.

## 1. The compatible family and its actual centroid

Fix d>=1 and put Q=[0,1]^(d-1), with the point convention when d=1. At
integer indices 0,1,2 use

    K_0=K_2=[0,1] x Q,       K_1=[0,3/2] x Q.

Let C be their convex hull in R x R^d. This is a full-dimensional convex
body. Its only integer fibers are exactly these three: the endpoint fibers
are extreme slices, and every mixture at index 1 belongs to K_1 because
(K_0+K_2)/2=K_0 subset K_1.

The mixed volumes are 1,3/2,1, with total M=7/2. Their individual
continuous centroids are (1/2,1/2,...), (3/4,1/2,...), (1/2,1/2,...).
The actual mixed centroid is

    g=(1,17/28,1/2,...,1/2).

Consider the closed tested cap H={x_1>=17/28}, which contains g on its
boundary. Both endpoint fiber centroids are strictly outside this cap.

## 2. Every nonnegative-cap-mean integer-centered component is proportional

Suppose the mixed-volume measure mu has a finite decomposition

    mu=sum_j mu_j,

where each nonzero mu_j has a density constant on each of the three full
fibers. Assume that every component's base centroid is integer and its
mean tested-cap coordinate x_1-17/28 is nonnegative. The latter condition
places its centroid in H and is the natural sign condition for applying
a through-component-centroid cap Jensen bound to this tested cap.

Write its fiber masses as m_0,m_1,m_2. Its base mean belongs to [0,2].
An integer mean 0 forces m_1=m_2=0; an integer mean 2 forces m_0=m_1=0.
In either case the continuous x_1 mean is 1/2<17/28, contrary to the sign
condition. Hence every component's base centroid is 1, and m_0=m_2=m.

Its unnormalized mean tested-cap coordinate is

    m(1/2-17/28)+m_1(3/4-17/28)+m(1/2-17/28)
       =(4m_1-6m)/28.

Thus m_1>=3m/2 for every component. Summing over components gives
sum_j m=1 and sum_j m_1=3/2. The nonnegative differences must consequently
all be zero. Therefore

    (m_0,m_1,m_2)=m(1,3/2,1)

in every component. Dividing by the actual fiber volumes proves
mu_j=m mu. In particular every component has precisely the same full
centroid g. This conclusion holds for any finite number of components,
not merely two.

## 3. Exact limitation for the effective-count Jensen mechanism

The effective fiber count of the original family is

    N_eff=M^(d+1)/[2+(3/2)^(1+1/d)]^d.

For any positive fiber volumes, sum a_z^(1+1/d)<=a_max^(1/d) M, so

    N_eff>=M/a_max=7/3>2.

For d=1 the exact value is 49/17. Thus this family is outside the
N_eff<=2 range of the own-fiber conditional Jensen theorem.

Every permitted centered decomposition above is merely a scalar splitting
of the original measure. The normalized conditional expectation and the
Jensen output point remain unchanged in every component. Multiplying its
bound by each scalar and summing reproduces the original bound, rather
than improving the effective fiber count or producing disjoint output
fibers. Hence this whole-fiber decomposition strategy cannot remove the
effective-count obstruction, even in the nonheavy three-fiber regime
b<2a singled out by the conditional centroid case split.

A partition that selects different subsets inside each fiber need not
satisfy this rigidity. Such a partition is outside the present obstruction,
but its conditional tail-root expectation is no longer automatically the
full-fiber identity d a_z^(1/d)/(d+1). No claim about the feasibility or
strength of such more general partitions is made here. The actual OC
conditional-centroid inequality is not disproved by this example.
